# Grosslytics (grosslytics.com)

> Revenue analytics for founders: credits each payment to the channel that brought the buyer, and reports revenue after payment-provider fees and ad spend.

## What it does
- Attributes sales from Stripe, Razorpay, Polar, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Cashfree, Gumroad, PayPal, Dodo Payments and RevenueCat (verified webhooks) to marketing channels. Sales tax is excluded from revenue.
- Counts AI crawler requests (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot…) per page, reported server-side to `POST /api/crawl`.
- Optional click map script (`/c.js`) for pricing and checkout pages: clicks, dead clicks, rage clicks, and buyers per element.
- Reads DataFast, Plausible and Umami goal syntax; imports past Stripe payments; imports ad spend from CSV.
- Attribution models: first touch, last touch, and linear (50/50 between first and last touch).
- Net revenue: subtracts an estimated gateway fee per payment, and ad spend per channel.
- Names traffic that other tools call "Direct": in-app browsers (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, Telegram, X), AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot), and shared links vs typed URLs.
- Live visitors and sales over WebSockets (Cloudflare Durable Objects).
- Built-in MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf.

## Setup
- Tracker (1.5 KB Brotli, no cookies, stores a random visitor ID in localStorage):
  `<script defer src="https://grosslytics.com/g.js" data-site-id="YOUR_SITE_ID"></script>`
- Stripe, Polar, Lemon Squeezy, Gumroad and Dodo Payments checkout links are tagged automatically. PayPal uses custom_id, Cashfree order_tags.visitor_id, RevenueCat the subscriber attribute visitor_id. Paddle requires custom_data.visitor_id via its checkout integration; Razorpay requires notes.visitor_id.
- Stripe events: checkout.session.completed, invoice.paid, invoice_payment.paid, charge.refunded (full refunds).
- One reporting currency per site: USD, EUR, GBP or INR; different currencies are never summed.
- Webhooks: `POST /api/webhooks/{stripe|razorpay|polar|paddle|lemonsqueezy|cashfree|gumroad|paypal|dodo|revenuecat}?siteId=YOUR_SITE_ID` (signature required; Gumroad uses a key in the URL).
- Self-host on Cloudflare: step-by-step at /start/. Full docs: /docs/.

## API (requires `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>`)
- `GET /api/stats?siteId=…&range=24h|7d|30d|90d&model=first|last|linear`: channel stats.
- `GET /api/stats/journey/{visitorId}?siteId=…`: one visitor's event timeline.
- MCP (Streamable HTTP): `/api/mcp?site=YOUR_SITE_ID`. Tools: query_channel_roas, inspect_unmasked_direct, get_ai_search_citations, get_buyer_journeys, compare_buyer_reading_time.

## Pricing
- Self-host: $0, open source (AGPL-3.0), your own Cloudflare account
- Indie Cloud: $5.99/month
- Lifetime: $29 one time. One-command installer and updates (no git or Bun), priority email support, and a commercial license without AGPL obligations

## Compared with alternatives (competitor facts from their websites, checked 2026-11-06)
- DataFast: also revenue-first with MCP; supports Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, Polar, Shopify; from $9/month. Grosslytics adds Razorpay and Paddle, fee deduction, and self-hosting. Tracker 4.5 KB vs 1.5 KB.
- DataBull: also self-hosted on Cloudflare with MCP; supports Stripe, Polar, Dodo, Creem; $49 once or hosted from $9/month. Both support Dodo; Grosslytics adds Razorpay, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy and fee deduction. Tracker 6.4 KB vs 1.5 KB.
- Plausible: private web analytics, open source, 1.1 KB tracker, from $9/month; revenue via custom events. Grosslytics adds payment-provider attribution and net revenue.
- Google Analytics 4: free and deep; gtag.js is 125 KB and uses cookies. Grosslytics is 1.5 KB with no cookies.

- [5 Best DataBull Alternatives for Paddle & Net Revenue](https://grosslytics.com/compare/databull-alternative.md): Compare five DataBull alternatives for Paddle, Razorpay, attribution and hosting. See license costs, fee estimates and the limits of each approach.
- [DataFast vs DataBull vs Grosslytics: Costs & Features](https://grosslytics.com/compare/datafast-vs-databull.md): Compare DataFast, DataBull and Grosslytics across 12 practical criteria, with annual cost scenarios, attribution definitions and a measured local tracker build.
- [Plausible vs Grosslytics: SaaS Revenue Tracking Compared](https://grosslytics.com/compare/plausible-alternative.md): Compare Plausible revenue goals with Grosslytics payment webhooks, including renewals, refunds, observed LTV and the difference between payments and MRR.
- [PostHog vs Grosslytics: Focused Revenue Attribution](https://grosslytics.com/compare/posthog-alternative.md): Compare PostHog with lightweight revenue analytics for Stripe attribution: scope, setup, pricing, measured tracker size and the reporting you give up.
- [How to Track Stripe Revenue by Traffic Source](https://grosslytics.com/blog/stripe-revenue-attribution.md): Connect Stripe Checkout and Payment Links to visitor sources, configure signed webhooks and verify fees, renewals and attribution limits in Grosslytics.
- [How to Track Polar & Dodo Payments Revenue by Channel](https://grosslytics.com/blog/polar-dodo-payments-analytics.md): Connect Polar, Dodo Payments and Lemon Squeezy checkouts to visitor sources using provider-specific metadata and signed webhooks, with renewal and refund limits.
- [How to Attribute Razorpay Payments to Traffic Sources](https://grosslytics.com/blog/razorpay-revenue-attribution.md): Connect Razorpay Standard Checkout payments to UTMs with payment notes and signed payment.captured events. Understand Payment Link, subscription and currency limits.
- [How to Track Paddle Revenue & Observed LTV by Source](https://grosslytics.com/blog/paddle-revenue-attribution.md): Attribute Paddle Billing transactions to visitor sources with customData and signed webhooks. Learn the limits of fee estimates, recurring receipts and observed LTV.
- [How to Self-Host Revenue Analytics on Cloudflare D1](https://grosslytics.com/blog/cloudflare-d1-web-analytics.md): Deploy Grosslytics on Cloudflare Workers and D1 in five steps. Understand free-tier limits, queue costs, source and licensed install paths, and verification.
- [How to Track ChatGPT Traffic Through to Real Revenue](https://grosslytics.com/blog/track-chatgpt-traffic-revenue.md): Identify ChatGPT visits by tag and referrer, carry the visitor into checkout and match payments. Includes a Stripe sandbox test and the limits of the data.
